brief: Last week's AI-led selloff drove the S&P 500 to its worst week since April 2025 (-2.68%), with semiconductors (-12.15%) and CoreWeave (-15.44%) hit hardest. Japan's Nikkei (-9.25%) had its worst week since March 2020, while Europe's smaller tech exposure limited the STOXX 600 to a small gain. Easing fears of Middle East escalation drove Brent down 13.32% to $98.32/bbl, and that risk-off tone plus falling oil pulled down global bond yields and lifted gold to its best week since August. Friday's October jobs report (+165k vs +70k expected, unemployment down to 4.1%) helped markets recover, and Asian equities are rallying this morning, led by Taiwan's Taiex (+4.94%) after regulator confidence measures, though an internal investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is capping gains. This week's US focus shifts to October CPI, which DB forecasts decelerating to 0.20% month-on-month for both headline and core, and to PPI, against a heavy Fed speaker slate. DB still expects 25bp rate hikes in December and March. Separately, DB's asset-allocation team finds Q3 global earnings growth eased to 33% from Q2's 38% but remains historically strong, led by an accelerating Europe (28%, a four-year high) narrowing its growth gap with the US.
